subject: Interpretation of the effective number of parameters

messages.author: e75d1d4342d59946
messages.subject: Interpretation of the effective number of parameters
parts:
I am fitting a simple GLMM with one continuous (Year) variate and a five level factor.  I am fitting a model with the following formula:

Response = alpha0_i _ alpha1_i . Year + alpha2_i . Year:habitat

My expectation was to fit an intercept, a difference in the intercept for the habitat class 2 to 5 and a Year slope for the first level of the habitat and four estimates of the differences in the slope for habitat 2 to 5.  

A total of ten parameters.  The number of p.eff that is reported is around 44.  The table of fixed parameters shows the number of estimates as I expeced.  

As with any model I fit I am sceptical but can anyone suggest what I should be reading to enlighten me as to the interpretation of the estimated number of effective parameters?

Nick.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Interpretation of the effective number of parameters
parts:
both DIC and WAIC has its own def of p.eff, and add to this, there are
various estimates of these,

like

> r=inla(y ~ 1, data=data.frame(y=1:10), control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,
waic=TRUE))
> r$waic$p.eff
[1] 1.675467946
> r$dic$p.eff
[1] 1.964058407
>


see attached.

I think the WAIC one is more reasonable (and the estimate used in INLA
is the variance of the score; see the attached paper).

what is Eff.Num.Parameters? well, its 'what you define it to be'. its
more a 'concept/idea', as there is no objective definition in general
(maybe in the Gaussian case only). its like two Normal random variables
with correlation rho. if rho=0 we have two independent ones (like
p.eff=2), and iff |rho|=1 we have two perferct dependent ones (like
p.eff=1), and inbetween we have something between 1 and 2.
